cards.explanation: The answer is that they will not enter into temptation. Jesus tells them, “Pray that you will not enter into temptation.” No long speech and no fine print, friends, just one clear thing to pray. He says it again in verse 46.

The answer is False. The text says Jesus prays, “Father, if You are willing, take this cup from Me. Yet not My will, but Yours be done.” So after the ask, He doesn't push for His own will, friends. He prays for the Father's will to be done.
The answer is an angel. Verse 43 says an angel from heaven appeared to Him and strengthened Him. He's out there praying alone, and heaven sends help. I think that's a quiet kind of kindness, friends.

The answer is True. The text says that in His anguish, He prayed more earnestly, “…and His sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground.” I think this one hurts to read, friends. It tells us how heavy this night was for Him.
The answer is asleep. Verse 45 says Jesus found them asleep, exhausted from sorrow. Then He asks, “Why are you sleeping?” That question comes in verse 46, friends.
The answer is sorrow. The text says the disciples were “…exhausted from sorrow.” This was no ordinary nap, friends. It was a heavy night for them.

The answer is kiss Him. Verse 47 says Judas “…approached Jesus to kiss Him.” It's a greeting people know well, friends, and it's what he walks up to do in front of the whole crowd. In verse 48, Jesus answers him with a question about it.

The answer is the servant of the high priest. Verse 50 says one of them struck the servant of the high priest. The high priest was the top priest, friends. The text doesn't name the swordsman or the servant here.
The answer is right ear. Verse 50 says the sword cut off the servant's right ear. The text is exact about which side, friends. That's the ear Jesus touches in verse 51.
The answer is True. Verse 51 says Jesus “…touched the man’s ear and healed him.” Just before that, He says, “No more of this!” In the middle of the arrest, friends, He heals the servant.

The answer is an outlaw. Jesus asks, “Have you come out with swords and clubs as you would against an outlaw?” It's a pointed question, friends. He's not hiding and He's not fighting, and He lets them see the picture.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “Every day I was with you in the temple courts, and you did not lay a hand on Me.” So all those days in the temple, friends, no hands laid on Him. He says it to the chief priests, temple officers, and elders who had come for Him.
The answer is the power of darkness. Jesus says, “But this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness.” It's a heavy line, friends, and He says it plainly. I'd read it slowly.
